regions.name: flow_near_wake
regions.why: The near-wake requirement volume is currently uncovered (configured_volume_coverage 0.0). This box matches the requirement bounds exactly. Level 3 gives h = 0.375/2^3 = 0.046875 m, which satisfies the required max_cell_axis_span_metres = 0.0875 m, whereas level 2 (0.09375 m) would violate it. Level 3 equals the global surface level, so no level jump is introduced at the body surface and the cells merge smoothly into the existing 0.09375 m distance shell.

regions.name: flow_far_wake
regions.why: The far-wake requirement volume is also uncovered (coverage 0.0). Level 2 gives h = 0.375/2^2 = 0.09375 m, under the required 0.175 m span cap, and is deliberately one level coarser than the near wake to bound cost of the slowly recovering deficit, matching the stated mechanism that far-wake transport is coarsenable. It is the same size as the existing 0.28125 m distance shell, so the wake box merges without a stair-step.

regions.name: flow_aft_shear_core
regions.why: Mechanism, not score-chasing: the dimensionless estimate discharges an aft-body boundary layer of about 0.0489 m, which is only ~1.04 level-3 cells (0.046875 m), so the emerging shear layer and velocity-deficit edge behind the trailing edge would be smeared over a single cell. Level 4 halves the cell to 0.0234375 m (~2 cells across the estimated discharge thickness) in the first 1.0 m of wake, where the cross-stream gradient is steepest, while leaving the rest of the near wake at level 3 and the far wake at 2. Lateral extent is kept identical to the near-wake box so the shear layer is not clipped by a lateral refinement boundary; the only level change is a single 4->3 step in streamwise direction, within n_cells_between_levels = 3. Level 4 is within +2 of the global surface level 3. This is a hypothesis-driven resolution increase expected to matter only for the near-field deficit; it is not evidence that the wake is accurately resolved.

regions.name: repair_0
regions.why: actual layer deficit concentrated in measured boundary faces

advisor.hypothesis: Restore the best measured anchor (plan:605313bf946a3459, coverage 0.8983, 7 layers, y+ intact, quality n_failed=0) and repair the LOCAL, not global, defect. Round0→round1 evidence: 8→7 layers changed coverage 0.0033→0.8983, i.e. per-face extrusion is near all-or-nothing; round1 extruded 8468/8584 faces but 11.7% of area sits at 0-4 layers. Clusters layer_shortfall:0 (x≈-1.59..-1.01) and layer_shortfall:1 (x≈1.13..1.59) are the fore/aft cap bands where the requested 0.016 m stack fits by >25x (median local feature 0.43 m), so the block is NOT space: it is column suppression from colliding/rapidly-rotating wall normals near the blunt caps (my round-0 attempt with feature_angle 150 + stronger normal smoothing still landed at 0.8581, so angle relaxation alone is not the lever). New causal mechanism: give the extruder more iterative room and a stricter medial/first-face criterion consistent with a displacementMedialAxis mover, and add one conservative MEDIAL-distance-aware n_grow=1 so neighbouring columns are stopped coherently instead of each face zeroing independently. Do not touch first height (estimated y+ p50 = 50.0 exact), surface level, or the wake boxes.
advisor.expected_change: Body-area fraction with ≥5 actual layers moves from 0.898 (anchor) / 0.858 (current failed) toward ≥0.90; the 0-4 layer bands at layer_shortfall:0 and layer_shortfall:1 shrink. Fidelity stays accepted (p99 0.00126 m vs 0.015 m), first_height stays 0.0012379 m so estimated y+ p50 stays 50.0, cells stay well inside the 2e6 budget. Uncertainty: coverage gain per iteration is not measured and n_grow may shift the deficit partly to adjacent faces; if coverage still fails, the remaining lever is the snap/wall-normal field, not global refinement.
counterevidence: round0 with 8 layers reached only 0.0033 coverage — layer count alone is not the lever; round1 with 7 layers reached 0.898

layer_shortfall:0/1 lie where the requested stack (~0.016-0.02 m) is >25x smaller than the measured median local feature 0.43 m, so this is extrusion suppression, not an out-of-space regime
round1's repair_0 level-4 box over the body did not lift coverage above 0.90 — purely geometric refinement is not the mechanism

n_outer_iter partitions layers and is not a retry counter

tightening max_thickness_to_medial_ratio below 0.3 to force longer, more uniform columns

actions.why: plan:605313bf946a3459 is the eligible measured anchor closest to the gate (layer_coverage 0.8983, fidelity accepted, native quality accepted n_failed 0) and its 7-layer / feature_angle 60 / min_medial_axis_angle 90 / n_outer_iter 1 layer_parameters become the baseline for the patch below, not the current 0.858 spec.

Residual deficit is confined to the cap bands layer_shortfall:0 / layer_shortfall:1, where the stack fits by >25x, so the columns are being stopped, not running out of space. Keep the anchor's feature_angle 60 (my earlier 150 made coverage worse: 0.858 vs 0.898) and keep the same first height to preserve estimated y+ p50 = 50.0. Give the medial-axis mover more contraction/relaxation iterations and one extra outer pass so the extrusion direction field can converge across the rapidly rotating cap normals, and re-enable a conservative n_grow=1 with a slightly relaxed medial angle so neighbouring points are stopped together instead of each face zeroing its own column. max_thickness_to_medial_ratio 0.3 and max_face_thickness_ratio 0.5 are unchanged (native mover shows no thickness truncation), so the first layer, stack height and y+ estimate are untouched.

The extruder's immediate inputs are the snapped wall-point field and its normal estimate; the failures are local, so improve the snapped field's smoothness rather than moving points far. Keep tolerance 2.0 (fidelity p99 0.00126 m vs 0.015 m tolerance), raise n_solve_iter 40→80 and n_feature_snap_iter 10→20, and add n_smooth_patch 3→5 with n_relax_iter 5→8 so the cap wall normals are coherent before extrusion.
